WHAT WAS AUTHORED: a configuration-only RosDriver for the pinned CBF demo node DroneCBFSim, selected from the repository's concrete ROS 2 runtime. The node creates a 10 Hz timer (drone_simulation/CBF_Demo/cbf_sim.py:71-72), advances a precomputed trajectory and publishes nav_msgs/msg/Odometry on the relative true_pose topic (cbf_sim.py:18,53-54,125-159). It imports tutorial_interfaces.srv.ResetSim and creates the service on /drone<my_id>/ResetSim (cbf_sim.py:33,74-77); ResetSim.srv declares reset bool and cbf_param float32 requests and a done bool response (tutorial_interfaces/srv/ResetSim.srv:1-4). reset_callback resets i, updates cbf_param, regenerates the trajectory and LQR sequence, zeros tru_pose, destroys and recreates the timer, and sets response.done=True (cbf_sim.py:194-232). The launch file runs the node in namespace drone1 with my_id 1 (drone_simulation/launch/single_agent_cbf_launch.py:17-25), so the resolved topic is /drone1/true_pose and the service is /drone1/ResetSim. The service binding uses the /ResetSim token shown in the source and therefore requires the operator to remap /drone1/ResetSim to /ResetSim (or expose the same root name); that remap is a deployment assumption, not an upstream Fact. The pose and twist are exposed as read-only resource state from the same Odometry topic. The reset is an x-cap extension with input reset bool and cbf_param number; cbf_param is Limit.operator_required because the clone states no numeric range and the launch/README 15 is a configurable default, not a bound. site-limits.example.json is an illustrative operator overlay, not a device fact.

WHY BLOCKED: the node creates no pause, stop, hold, disarm or shutdown service/action. ResetSim resets the trajectory and recreates the 10 Hz timer, so the simulation resumes after the callback; the returned done flag acknowledges the callback, not a stopped state. The package deliberately does not declare ResetSim as a safe-state action or e-stop and does not declare estop_physical_ref. With no native stop, the stock e-stop returns MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED and G6.ESTOP_FAILED; the MHS-Sim CL3 SAFE-028 test fails because safe_state.achieved is false; G9 is not run. This is a genuine upstream stop gap: at R1 the conformance suite requires the e-stop to reach the device and its safe state, and a software latch alone is not evidence that an external ROS controller stopped. The task rules forbid claiming the reset as safety or making the fake complete instantly to pretend the stop is proven. I did not use the alternative /drone1/DroneSim step service from sim_service.py either: it has the same no-stop gap and its response (reward, state, done; tutorial_interfaces/srv/DroneSim.srv:4-6) has no application success/error field. done is a Gymnasium terminal flag, not a success flag; the RosDriver requires an application success predicate for an effectful call, and declaring the effectful step as operation=read would weaken the contract. The step service is therefore not declared read-only or given an invented success field.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card hints name RapidTrajectory/SingleAxisTrajectory reads, writes and resets. Those are internal pure-Python trajectory helpers (drone_simulation/drone_simulation/quadrocoptertrajectory.py), not the selected ROS 2 runtime interface; the card's candidate classes (cap.sensing.read.v1, cap.device.configure.v1, cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1) do not bind ResetSim, a service invoke with reset/cbf_param and a done response. The extension x-cap.patilunmesh.reset.v1 is used with an inline schema, and the pose/twist are resource reads, not a motion command. The card's mock_strategy preferred upstream-sim was not executed: the pinned clone is read-only and this session neither imports nor runs it; the fake is a ROS-free recording stand-in, not a captured transcript.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the selected DroneCBFSim node (drone_simulation/CBF_Demo/cbf_sim.py) advances a precomputed trajectory on a 10 Hz timer (71-72, 125-163) and serves only ResetSim, whose callback replans, zeroes the pose, recreates the timer and answers done=true (194-232), so the drone restarts its trajectory instead of stopping; no pause or stop exists, and the effectful reset leaves the stock e-stop at G6.ESTOP_FAILED and, at the card's R1 floor, G8 SAFE-028 with the latch held (HELPER_MISSING). The ResetSim and Odometry types, the operator_required cbf_param and the ROS 2 fake shapes match the source. Defects left for the next author: the node registers the absolute name '/drone' + str(my_id) + '/ResetSim' (75-77), which the shipped launch (my_id 1) makes /drone1/ResetSim in any namespace, but the binding configures /ResetSim, a fact calls the name relative, and the comments ask the operator to remap it (the gate accepts the suffix, so it cannot catch this); /drone1/true_pose is published only while the trajectory index is below 499 (132-156), so about 50 s after start or a reset the pose and twist resource reads fail NOT_READY and every command waits for them, which the always-answering fake hides; and the 10 Hz timer fact cites 125-159, while the timer is created on 71-72.
